title: Refactor decision graph and implement fallback throttler
creator: Connor Lee
description:
Problem: The smart routing decision pipeline has accumulated ad-hoc heuristics and blocking locks that cause tail-latency spikes under regional surge. Multiple fallback mechanisms (circuit breakers, region failover, model-variant fallback) are applied in scattered places which makes reasoning about throttling and escalation difficult. Several downstream regressions were traced to contention in the policy evaluation hotpath and to unbounded concurrent fallback attempts when a region partially degrades.

Goal: Consolidate the routing decision model into an explicit, in-memory decision graph, and introduce a central fallback throttler component. The decision graph will be deterministic, composable, and auditable; the throttler will cap in-flight fallback attempts per region/model variant and expose metrics/priority queues. The work should reduce p95/p99 routing latency, remove a set of global locks, and make fallbacks predictable during partial outages.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Implement a DecisionGraph abstraction (immutable nodes + deterministic evaluation order) and migrate the policy evaluator to use it.
- Replace scattered fallback triggers with calls to a new FallbackThrottler service that enforces configurable concurrency limits and exponential backoff policies.
- Remove one global mutex in route selection and migrate to per-shard state with atomic updates.
- Add tracing spans and telemetry for decision-graph evaluation time, throttler queue lengths, per-region fallback delays, and throttled-counts.
- Integration tests that simulate regional congestion and assert throttler behaviour and correct fallback ordering.
- Canary rollout plan with feature-flagged activation and runtime knobs for limits per-customer tier.

Acceptance Criteria:
- p95 routing latency improves by >= 12% under the synthetic regional surge test (see perf harness).
- No global route selection mutex held longer than 2ms in steady-state test.
- Throttler exposes metrics: fallback_in_flight, fallback_throttled, fallback_queue_depth and they match simulated load expectations.
- End-to-end canary (5% of traffic) shows no increase in failed requests and correct fallback ordering in 7-day observation window.
- All new code covered by unit tests and integration tests; PR passes security and load checks.

Workplan & Timeline:
- Spike (3 days): prototype DecisionGraph and safe migration path; measure perf on synthetic traces.
- Implementation (2 weeks): DecisionGraph core, FallbackThrottler, telemetry hooks, and migration shims.
- Testing (1 week): unit/integration harness, chaos scenarios for partial regional failures.
- Canary & Rollout (1 week): gradual enablement with monitoring dashboards and rollback playbook.

Notes & Rationale:
- DecisionGraph gives a single canonical representation of routing logic so future policy changes can be validated against the graph before runtime.
- Central throttler prevents thundering-herd fallbacks that amplify regional issues and helps enforce per-customer SLA isolation.
- Moving away from a global mutex reduces contention and unlocks higher QPS on Dedicated pools.

Artifacts & Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/SG-DecisionGraph+Design
- Perf harness (internal repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-perf-harness/pulls/42
- Proto changes (RFC): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1q2exampleproto
- Observatory dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/routing/decision-graph-throttler

Rollout & Safety Controls:
- Feature flag gated: routing.decision_graph.enabled (can be scoped by region and team).
- Throttler defaults conservative: global fallback concurrency=50, region default=10; can increase via console.
- Automated rollback: if fallback_throttled increases >20% and error_rate >2x baseline in canary, roll back to old path automatically.

Implementation Notes:
- Avoid changing public API signatures for route selection; keep migration shims to flip from old evaluator to new DecisionGraph.
- Use lock-free ring buffers for the throttler queue where possible; fall back to per-shard mutex with fast paths for empty queues.
- Add feature to snapshot decision graph for offline audits and explainability.
comments: 2025-10-16 - Connor Lee: Kickoff spike started. Built a minimal DecisionGraph prototype (node + deterministic evaluator) and ran it against a recorded 24h trace from last June regional outage. Early numbers show 10-14% reduction in evaluator p95 under synthetic replay.
2025-10-20 - Asha Patel: Design review with PM and Observability. Agreed on throttler metrics and rollback thresholds. PM requested per-customer limit knobs exposed in the console; added to scope.

2025-10-24 - Miguel Santos (code review): Noted that the initial graph node representation may allocate during evaluation; suggested pre-allocating node arrays per request size and using indices to avoid GC pressure. Added as implementation task.

2025-10-28 - Asha Patel: Implemented FallbackThrottler prototype with per-region semaphores and queue. Local load test simulating 2x surge shows throttled events but overall downstream systems stay within capacity.

2025-10-30 - QA: Added integration tests that simulate a region returning 429s and assert that throttler prevents >N concurrent fallback attempts. Two flaky tests identified around timing; flakiness tracked in ENG-786542.
2025-11-01 - Release engineering: Protobuf schema change noted; marked as non-breaking but requires clients to tolerate missing fields. Added migration note to release-1.20 notes.
2025-11-02 - Asha Patel: Started canary rollout plan. Preparing dashboards and alert rules. Next: open PR for DecisionGraph migration and request load test on staging with 1M requests/day trace.
